newsitem.title: ITALY: Two opposition MPs move to Dini's Italian Renewal.
newsitem.headline: Two opposition MPs move to Dini's Italian Renewal.

text.p: Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini's centrist Italian Renewal party said on Monday two opposition deputies had joined its ranks in the lower house of parliament.

The defections by Nicola Miraglia De Giudice from the hard-right National Alliance (AN) party and Stefano Bastianoni from the centrist CCD-CDU group will increase the centre-left government's majority in the Chamber of Deputies.

They are also essential to Italian Renewal because it needs at least 20 deputies to form its own parliamentary group with the right to name a representative to a new commission on constitutional reform formed by the two houses of parliament.
A party spokesman said the new members would take Italian Renewal's strength to 21 deputies from 19.
Dini created Italian Renewal before the April general election last year while serving as stop-gap prime minister.
It had 26 deputies after the election but a split cut its strength to 14. The other 12 remain loyal to the government.
Two members of Berlusconi's Forza Italia switched to Italian Renewal earlier this month. Three pro-government deputies also joined the party from other forces, bringing the total to 19.
AN and CCD-CDU are part of media magnate Silvio Berlusconi's centre-right opposition Freedom Alliance bloc.
The centre ground of Italian politics has been fragmented and in a state of flux since the demise of the long dominant Christian Democrat party, embroiled in the country's corruption scandals.
Dini is among centrist leaders pushing for a consolidation of the centre across the government-opposition divide.
